AFFAIRES.INTRO_TEXT: Every project of the portfolio: budget, remaining to invoice (RAF) and status of each one. Follow the guide for a quick tour.
AFFAIRES.NEW_TEXT: « New project » opens the creation wizard, step by step. The project stays a draft until the wizard is validated, then becomes « In progress ». Reserved to people who manage projects.
AFFAIRES.KPIS_TEXT: Active projects (« In progress »), total remaining (RAF), total budget and « Suspended » projects. They cover every project of the filter, not only the page shown; the note under the figure reads « all projects » or « filters applied ».
AFFAIRES.TOOLBAR_TEXT: Search by reference or title. « Filters » narrows by status, client, country, manager, billing mode or start date. The buttons on the right switch between cards and table.
AFFAIRES.LIST_TEXT: Click a project to open its file. A card shows budget, RAF, invoiced and WIP. The bin only shows on drafts. Coming back from the file, you find your filters, sort and page again.
AFFAIRES.STATUS_TEXT: Draft: creation started, not validated yet — the only status that can be deleted. Configured: set up, not in progress yet. In progress: the active project, the only one accepting new extra works. Suspended: no more invoicing. Closed: no invoicing nor changes. Archived: kept for history, no changes.

AFFAIRE_NEW.INTRO_TEXT: The wizard creates the project in 6 steps. The guide shows them one by one without saving anything: when it closes, the wizard is back where you left it.
AFFAIRE_NEW.RAIL_TEXT: The rail shows where you are. A step already passed reopens with a click; the next ones stay locked until the previous one is complete.
AFFAIRE_NEW.NEXT_TEXT: « Next » saves the step and moves on; it stays greyed out while the step is incomplete. Once step 2 is passed, the project exists as a draft. On the last step, « Activate project » sets it « In progress » and locks its billing mode.
AFFAIRE_NEW.HEADER_TEXT: Under the title, chips sum up what was entered: entity, client, billing mode and budget. The reference shows as soon as it exists.
AFFAIRE_NEW.DRAFTS_TEXT: You can leave the wizard at any time after step 2: the project stays a draft. This link opens the list of drafts; open yours to pick up where you left off.

DOC.S1_TEXT: Optional. Search a DOC360 or Interco project to link the project to its contract documents and reuse its base data. With no project to link, go straight to the next step.
DOC.S2_TEXT: Entity (suggested from your country, editable until creation), client with validated KYC, title, billing mode, forecast budget (> 0), contract currency and at least one client contact — the one who will receive the invoices. « Next » creates the project as a draft.
DOC.S3_TEXT: Depending on the mode: fixed price — CTR / BPE / TQC split adding up to exactly 100 %; time & materials — at least one resource with a rate above 0; deliverables — at least one saved deliverable. The mode can no longer change after activation.
DOC.S4_TEXT: Add each manager with an activity and an allocated budget (> 0). A manager cannot have the same activity twice, and the allocations must add up to exactly the forecast budget.
DOC.S5_TEXT: Billing start date and contract duration in months. The date can be in the future: it triggers the first issue.
DOC.S6_TEXT: Check each section; a passed step reopens from the rail. « Activate project » checks everything, sets the project « In progress » and opens its file.

AFFAIRE_DETAIL.INTRO_TEXT: Everything about a project in one place: its details on the left, its indicators and tabs on the right. This guide walks you through it; the tabs open on their own, and you get your tab back at the end.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.HEADER_TEXT: The title, the reference and the client. The badges show the status (Draft, In progress, Suspended, Closed…), the budget health (Optimal, Watch, Critical) and « Budget not validated » until the budget is validated. The « Projects » breadcrumb takes you back to the list.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.DETAILS_TEXT: The client, with the contract's entity and currency, then the contract (start date, budget, billing mode, budget validated, references), the selling entities, the managers, the client contacts and the notes.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.ACTIONS_TEXT: « New invoice » opens invoicing for this project, « New additional work » declares additional work, « Add expenses » records reimbursable expenses. At the bottom: « Edit project » (« Complete draft » for a draft) and the status badge, which you click to change it. « Validate budget » shows until it is validated, « Delete draft » only on a draft. The buttons shown depend on your rights.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.KPIS_TEXT: Backlog (what is left of the contract to invoice), Total invoiced (invoices not yet collected), Total collected (fully paid invoices), WIP (declared work) and TS (additional work added to the budget). Each tile’s (i) gives its exact calculation.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.TABS_TEXT: One part of the project per tab; the number is the count of TS, invoices or payments. WIP, Resources and Expense only show for some billing modes. The open tab is kept in the address (?tab=…): F5 or a shared link reopens the same one.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.OVERVIEW_TEXT: Three charts: Invoicing, WIP and Payments. Click a name to show it, Ctrl + click to combine several. « Filters » sets the period (current year by default), the granularity and the per-period or cumulative view; the (i) explains the chart shown. Clicking a bar opens that period’s invoices, payments or WIP. The chosen chart is kept in the address (cc=PAYMENTS for Payments).
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.TS_TEXT: The project’s TS: work sold on top of the contract. A TS goes through technical then commercial validation, then joins the budget automatically (it raises the remaining-to-invoice). A row’s ⋮ menu offers the allowed actions: validate, edit or delete before the validations, view, history. A TS can only be created on an In progress project.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.TS_WIP_TEXT: The progress of integrated or invoiced TS: pick a TS, declare the period’s progress (as a % or an amount), submit it, then enter the amount confirmed by the client. The history keeps every declaration.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.WIP_TEXT: The work in progress to validate before invoicing, by mode: Lump Sum, the cumulative progress rate (as a % or an amount); Time & Materials, the period’s Timesheet hours; Deliverables, each deliverable’s progress. Each declaration is submitted, then confirmed by the client.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.RESSOURCES_TEXT: Time & Materials project: the billed employees and their rate. « Add a resource », change a rate or deactivate a resource; a locked rate (🔒) can no longer be changed.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.DEPENSE_TEXT: Read only: the hours logged in Timesheet on the project and their estimated internal cost, per employee, with filters and Excel export.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.INVOICES_TEXT: The project’s invoices, with search, filters and export. « View » shows the details; « Edit » is only possible on a draft or returned invoice, and opens the invoice in « Invoices ».
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.PAYMENTS_TEXT: The payments received on the project’s invoices (date, invoice, method, reference, amount), read only. A payment is recorded from the invoice, with « Record a payment »; « Edit » opens « Collections ».
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.EXPENSES_TEXT: The project’s reimbursable expenses, whatever its billing mode. They are entered with « Add expenses »; those with the right validate or reject them here.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.DRAWER_TEXT: This button opens the panel of upcoming deadlines, alerts (remaining-to-invoice threshold) and recent activity of the project. A dot on the button signals an alert.
AFFAIRE_DETAIL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide any time from « Help & guides », at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

AFFAIRE_EDIT.INTRO_TEXT: Editing reuses the creation wizard, without the Origin step: General info, Billing, Managers, Schedule and Summary. The guide previews each step without saving anything; when it closes, you are back on the step you were on.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.HEADER_TEXT: The « Edit project » title, with the reference and the name. The badges sum up the project (entity, client, billing mode, budget) and follow your changes.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.RAIL_TEXT: The rail has five steps: the DOC360 origin can no longer change. On an active project, every step is open: click straight on the one to fix. On a draft you are completing, the steps unlock one by one, as at creation.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.S2_TEXT: Name, client, client contacts, billing mode, planned budget, currency, billing period, references and notes. The entity is « set at creation »: only an administrator can correct it. The billing mode can still change; the new mode is configured in the Billing step.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.S3_TEXT: The mode’s configuration: lump sum — CTR / BPE / TQC split adding up to exactly 100%; time & materials — the resources and their rate; deliverables — the list of deliverables. On an active project, existing resources are updated, not recreated.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.S4_TEXT: The managers, their activity and their allocated budget (> 0). The allocations must add up to exactly the planned budget: if you changed the budget in General info, adjust them here.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.S5_TEXT: Billing start date, contract length in months and first due date. The contractual end date is recomputed from the start date and the length.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.S6_TEXT: Review the project. On an active project, « Save » takes you back to its file: the steps were already saved one by one. On a draft, « Activate project » checks everything and moves it to « In progress ».
AFFAIRE_EDIT.NEXT_TEXT: « Next » saves the step shown straight away, then moves to the next one. It stays greyed out while the step is incomplete; the message under the form says what is missing. There is no overall save at the end.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.BACK_TEXT: « Previous » goes back one step. On the first step, « Cancel » takes you back to the project list. Only the input of the step shown is lost: the steps confirmed with « Next » stay saved.
AFFAIRE_EDIT.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

CLIENTS.INTRO_TEXT: The portfolio of invoiced clients: their revenue, their KYC and their projects in progress. This guide tours the page.
CLIENTS.NEW_TEXT: Opens the client creation wizard. The code and the name must be unique within the entity. The button only shows with the right to manage invoicing.
CLIENTS.KPIS_TEXT: Total Clients counts every client found (under the figure: the filtered country, else « All countries »). KYC Validated, Total Revenue and Active Clients only cover the page shown (« Current page »); Total Revenue is converted to euros to add up different currencies.
CLIENTS.TOOLBAR_TEXT: The search covers the client’s name, code and tax / VAT number. « Filters » combines sector, status (active / inactive), KYC status, client country, default currency and active projects. The icons on the right switch between cards and table; in the table, click a header to sort.
CLIENTS.LIST_TEXT: Each client shows its code, its sector or country, its total revenue (in its currency), its active projects (In progress), its payment terms in days and its country. A click opens its file. Back from the file, your filters, sort, page and view are kept.
CLIENTS.STATE_TEXT: A single badge: « Inactive » if the client is deactivated, else « KYC Validated » or « KYC pending ». A project can only be created for a client with a validated KYC. The KYC is validated, and the client deactivated, from its file.
CLIENTS.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

CLIENT_NEW.INTRO_TEXT: The wizard creates the client in 3 steps: Identification, Company details, Commercial terms. The guide shows them one by one without saving anything; when it closes, the wizard is where you left it.
CLIENT_NEW.HEADER_TEXT: The client’s name shows under the title as soon as it is typed; the badges sum up the input (industry, city, currency). The « Clients » breadcrumb goes back to the list.
CLIENT_NEW.RAIL_TEXT: The rail shows where you are. A step already seen reopens with a click; the next ones stay locked until you reach them with « Next ».
CLIENT_NEW.S1_TEXT: Client name and industry (required), client code and Tax ID / VAT. At creation, leave the code empty to have it generated. The code and the name must be unique within the entity.
CLIENT_NEW.S2_TEXT: The company’s address (address, city, postal code, country of origin, website), then its contacts: at least one, with a name. They are the ones attached to projects and receiving invoices; without an e-mail address, a contact receives no invoice. Only one contact is « primary ».
CLIENT_NEW.S3_TEXT: Payment term in days (0 to 365, 30 by default), default currency (TND, EGP, EUR or USD) and internal notes.
CLIENT_NEW.NEXT_TEXT: « Next » moves to the next step; nothing is saved yet. The client is created, with its contacts, in one go with « Create client » on the last step, which then opens its file. Its KYC is then « pending ».
CLIENT_NEW.BACK_TEXT: « Previous » goes back one step without losing anything. On the first step, « Cancel » goes back to the list: the input was not saved, so it is lost.
CLIENT_NEW.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

CLIENT_EDIT.INTRO_TEXT: Editing reuses the creation wizard, prefilled: Identification, Company details, Commercial terms. The guide previews each step without saving anything.
CLIENT_EDIT.RAIL_TEXT: Every step is open: click straight on the one to fix in the rail.
CLIENT_EDIT.S2_TEXT: The company’s address, then its contacts: add, edit or remove a contact. A removed contact is deactivated (it stays in the invoice history). Removal is refused for the primary contact or for a contact attached to a project in progress.
CLIENT_EDIT.NEXT_TEXT: « Next » moves from one step to the next without saving. Everything is saved at the end with « Save »: the client first, then its contacts one by one; you then go back to its file.
CLIENT_EDIT.BACK_TEXT: « Previous » goes back one step. On the first step, « Cancel » goes back to the client’s file without saving anything.

CLIENT_DETAIL.INTRO_TEXT: Everything about a client in one place: its identity and actions on the left, its figures and tabs on the right. This guide tours it; the tabs open by themselves, and you get yours back at the end.
CLIENT_DETAIL.HEADER_TEXT: The client’s name, with its code, country and industry. The badges give its status (Inactive, KYC Validated or KYC pending) and its payment term. The « Clients » breadcrumb goes back to the list, with your filters.
CLIENT_DETAIL.IDENTITY_TEXT: Code, country, address, industry, currency, payment term, Tax ID / VAT, website (clickable) and internal notes.
CLIENT_DETAIL.ACTIONS_TEXT: « New invoice » opens invoicing for this client. « Approve KYC » (or « Revoke KYC »), « Edit client » and « Block client » (or « Reactivate client ») need the right to manage invoicing.
CLIENT_DETAIL.KPIS_TEXT: Projects (all its projects, including those in progress), Total invoiced (excluding drafts and cancelled invoices), Collected (payments received) and Outstanding (invoiced minus collected), in the client’s currency.
CLIENT_DETAIL.TABS_TEXT: Overview, Contacts and Audit trail. The open tab is kept in the address (?tab=…): F5 or a shared link reopens the same one.
CLIENT_DETAIL.OVERVIEW_TEXT: The KYC approval card (date and author, or a reminder if missing), the related projects (Total, In progress, Completed) with « View projects », which opens the project list filtered on this client, and collection: the collected and outstanding shares of the total invoiced, with the observed average payment delay.
CLIENT_DETAIL.CONTACTS_TEXT: The client’s contacts: the « Primary » one, the e-mail address (without it, the contact receives no invoice) and the number of projects it is attached to. « Add a contact », edit or deactivate a contact; deactivated contacts are listed below, with « Reactivate ».
CLIENT_DETAIL.TRACE_TEXT: The client’s dates: creation, last change, KYC approval (date and author) and last activity.
CLIENT_DETAIL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

INVOICES.INTRO_TEXT: Every client invoice, from draft to payment. This guide tours the page and an invoice’s journey.
INVOICES.NEW_TEXT: Opens the creation wizard: project, lines, conditions, summary. The invoice starts as a draft; it has no number yet.
INVOICES.KPIS_TEXT: Total Invoiced, Pending (issued, sent or partly paid), Overdue (the same, past due) and Disputes. They only cover the page shown (« current page ») and are converted to euros; the small figure gives the number of invoices.
INVOICES.TOOLBAR_TEXT: The search covers the invoice number, the client and the project (reference or name). « Filters » combines status, issue period, client, project, « Overdue only », due period and min / max amount incl. tax. The icons on the right switch between grid and list; in the list, click a header to sort.
INVOICES.LIST_TEXT: Each invoice shows its reference and project, its client, its amount incl. tax, its status and its dates (issue, due, days overdue). A click opens its file. Back from it, your filters, sort, page and view are kept.
INVOICES.QUICK_TEXT: Without opening the file, each invoice offers the action of its step: « Approve invoice » (under review), « Issue invoice » (approved), « Mark as sent » (issued) and « Record a payment » (issued, sent or partly paid).
INVOICES.LIFECYCLE_TEXT: Draft → « Submit for approval » → Under review → decision: Approved, Returned (to fix and resubmit) or Cancelled (rejected) → « Issue invoice »: it gets its number (FAC-year-no.) and is e-mailed to the contacts → Sent → Partly paid → Paid. Alongside: Disputed and Credit issued.
INVOICES.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

INVOICE_NEW.INTRO_TEXT: The wizard builds the invoice in 4 steps: Project & Client, Lines, Conditions, Summary. Each step needs the previous one: the guide describes them here.
INVOICE_NEW.HEADER_TEXT: The badges sum up the input step by step: client, invoice type, number of lines and total incl. tax. The breadcrumb leads back to the list, or to the project / client file you came from.
INVOICE_NEW.RAIL_TEXT: The rail shows the current step. Clicking a previous step goes back to it; you cannot jump ahead, each step passing its data to the next.
INVOICE_NEW.S1_TEXT: Search for the project (name or number), then pick the invoice type (down payment, progress, final…) and, if needed, the related TS. The budget and available remaining-to-invoice show: an exhausted one blocks invoicing. The project must be In progress with a validated budget.
INVOICE_NEW.S2_TEXT: The lines to invoice: description, quantity, unit price excl. tax, VAT. Except for a down payment, an invoice created here can only carry reimbursable expenses (« + Add a reimbursable ») or unbilled WIP balances (« + Add an unbilled WIP balance »); progress, hours and deliverables go through WIP validation. Up to 3 deduction columns can be added.
INVOICE_NEW.S3_TEXT: Payment conditions, due date (suggested from the conditions, editable), purchase order (required for lump sum) and internal notes. The due date drives the payment reminders.
INVOICE_NEW.S4_TEXT: Review the client, the lines, the totals (excl. tax, incl. tax, net payable) and the preview of scheduled reminders. The amount excl. tax must not exceed the project’s remaining-to-invoice (RG12). Once saved, « Export as PDF » gives a preview marked DRAFT.
INVOICE_NEW.ACTIONS_TEXT: « Next » moves to the next step. On the summary, « Draft » saves the invoice to come back later; « Submit » saves it and sends it for approval. « Back » goes back one step, « Cancel » leaves without saving anything.
INVOICE_NEW.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

INVOICE_EDIT.INTRO_TEXT: The same wizard, prefilled. Two cases: a draft (freely editable), or an invoice already issued or sent with no payment, corrected while keeping its number (specific right required).
INVOICE_EDIT.ACTIONS_TEXT: For a draft: « Draft » saves, « Submit » saves and sends for approval. For an issued invoice: « Save changes » is the only button; the before / after is kept in the file’s « Modification history » tab.

INVOICE_DETAIL.INTRO_TEXT: Everything about an invoice: its identity and lifecycle on the left, its figures and tabs on the right. This guide tours it; the tabs open by themselves, and you get yours back at the end.
INVOICE_DETAIL.HEADER_TEXT: The invoice number (« Draft » until it is issued), the client and the project — the subtitle leads to the project — and the status badge.
INVOICE_DETAIL.IDENTITY_TEXT: Client, project, any TS, type, currency, issue and due dates, payment conditions, purchase order and notes.
INVOICE_DETAIL.ACTIONS_TEXT: The large button is the next step: « Submit for approval », « Confirm decision », « Issue invoice », « Mark as sent », « Record payment » or « Resolve dispute ». Depending on the status, « Edit draft », « Edit » (issued, no payment), « Return to sender », « Open a dispute », « Issue credit note », « View project » and « Export as PDF » are added.
INVOICE_DETAIL.KPIS_TEXT: The invoice’s progress through its journey (in %, from its status), its amount incl. tax (with excl. tax) and the remaining to pay, with the due date — in red when past.
INVOICE_DETAIL.TABS_TEXT: Billing lines, Reminders, Modification history and Timeline. The open tab is kept in the address (?tab=…).
INVOICE_DETAIL.LINES_TEXT: The lines, with search, then the total excl. tax, any deductions and the net payable.
INVOICE_DETAIL.REMINDERS_TEXT: The payment reminders scheduled from the due date (before, on the day, then after). They go out automatically every morning; « Suspend » pauses them, « Reactivate » resumes them. A dispute suspends them; full payment or a credit note stops them.
INVOICE_DETAIL.AUDIT_TEXT: Every event of the invoice, with its author, its comment and the changed fields (before / after), notably on a change after issue.
INVOICE_DETAIL.TRACE_TEXT: The key dates: creation, last change, issue, due date and full payment.
INVOICE_DETAIL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

COLLECTIONS.INTRO_TEXT: The list of your entity’s invoices to collect: issued, sent or partly paid, with their outstanding amount and lateness. Disputed, paid or draft invoices are not listed.
COLLECTIONS.KPIS_TEXT: Outstanding receivables (every amount still owed), Past due (the share past its due date), Collected this month (payments received since the 1st) and Past due 90+ days. Computed on all the entity’s invoices, not just the page; each tile’s (i) details the computation.
COLLECTIONS.TOOLBAR_TEXT: The search covers the client and the invoice number. « Filters »: project and client (by their ID), period — on the due date — and « Overdue only ». The icons on the right switch between grid and list; in the list, click a header to sort.
COLLECTIONS.LIST_TEXT: For each invoice: client, number, outstanding (of the amount incl. tax), due date and days late — orange beyond 30 days, red beyond 60. A click opens its collection file.
COLLECTIONS.REMINDER_TEXT: The last reminder sent for the invoice. Reminders go out automatically every morning based on the due date; they are suspended from the invoice’s collection file.
COLLECTIONS.RECON_TEXT: The « Bank reconciliation » button in the header is still disabled. The page exists at /finance/recouvrement/reconciliation: it has its own guide.
COLLECTIONS.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

RECONCILIATION.INTRO_TEXT: Import a bank statement, then match each transfer received with an invoice: confirming records the payment on the invoice.
RECONCILIATION.IMPORT_TEXT: Drop a file or click to pick it, then « Import ». Accepted formats: OFX (.ofx) and CAMT053 (.xml), 10 MB max. No CSV or Excel. On import, invoices are proposed automatically for each operation.
RECONCILIATION.MANUAL_TEXT: « + Manual entry » adds an operation without a file (date, amount, reference, description). It shows in the history as « Saisie manuelle » and also gets an automatic proposal.
RECONCILIATION.HISTORY_TEXT: Each import, with its format, date, and number of matched (✓) and unmatched (?) operations. Click an import to show its operations on the right.
RECONCILIATION.TRANSACTIONS_TEXT: The chosen import’s operations: date, reference, description, amount, status and proposed invoice. Statuses: Unmatched, Proposed, Confirmed, Partial, Rejected, Advance. ↻ refreshes the list.
RECONCILIATION.ACTIONS_TEXT: On a proposal: « Confirmer » records a payment of the transfer amount on the proposed invoice, « Partiel » assigns only part of it, « Rejeter » discards the proposal. On an unmatched operation: « Rapprocher » (pick the invoice yourself), « Partiel » or « Acompte ». A processed operation cannot be undone.
RECONCILIATION.UNMATCHED_TEXT: The total of operations still « Unmatched », by age (0 – 30 d, 31 – 60 d, 61 – 90 d, > 90 d) since their value date.
RECONCILIATION.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

COLLECTION_DETAIL.INTRO_TEXT: Tracking of an invoice to collect: its reminders, its payments and what remains owed. This guide tours it; the tabs open by themselves, and you get yours back at the end.
COLLECTION_DETAIL.HEADER_TEXT: The invoice number, its client and project, its status and, if late, the number of days.
COLLECTION_DETAIL.IDENTITY_TEXT: Client, project, issue and due dates, currency, reminder state (active or suspended) and date of the last reminder sent.
COLLECTION_DETAIL.ACTIONS_TEXT: « Record a payment », « Suspend reminders » (optional reason) or « Resume reminders » need the right to manage invoicing. « View invoice » and « View project » open their files.
COLLECTION_DETAIL.KPIS_TEXT: Invoiced amount (incl. tax), Collected (with the % of the amount), Outstanding and Overdue by (days) — « Up to date » if the due date has not passed.
COLLECTION_DETAIL.TABS_TEXT: Reminder schedule and Payments received. The open tab is kept in the address (?tab=…).
COLLECTION_DETAIL.REMINDERS_TEXT: Each planned reminder (stage and offset from the due date, D-7, D+7…), its scheduled date, sent date and status: Pending, Suspended (with the reason) or Sent. They go out automatically every morning.
COLLECTION_DETAIL.PAYMENTS_TEXT: The payments received: value date (and entry date), method and reference, note and amount; at the bottom, invoiced − collected = outstanding.
COLLECTION_DETAIL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

APPROVAL_QUEUE.INTRO_TEXT: This is where billing requests from projects (WIP, progress, deliverables, TS) and credit notes are approved. Approving a request creates the draft invoice. This guide opens the tabs by itself and gives yours back at the end.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.KPIS_TEXT: « Pending validation » counts every request to handle (lines, deliverable batches, credit notes). « Action history » counts the decisions loaded in the History tab (the latest 200). « Pending RF » does not concern these requests.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.TABS_TEXT: « Pending validation »: what awaits a decision. « History »: the log of decisions taken.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.SUBTABS_TEXT: Requests are grouped by mode: Lump sum, Time & materials, Deliverables and Extra Work. Each sub-tab’s figure gives the number of requests. Each table has its own search, filters (project, period, amount…), sort and paging.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.FORFAIT_TEXT: Progress declared on lump-sum projects (progress rate), one line per period: project, reference, period, amount excl. tax, status. Below, the credit notes of lump-sum invoices.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.REGIE_TEXT: The WIP of time & materials projects (Timesheet hours of the period, at the amount confirmed by the client), and their credit notes.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.LIVRABLE_TEXT: Deliverable batches: project, number of documents, amount excl. tax, billing date. A selection can only group batches of the same project: approval creates an invoice with one line per document.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.TS_TEXT: Progress of extra work (TS) integrated into the budget. Once invoiced at 100 %, the TS becomes Invoiced.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.ACTIONS_TEXT: Clicking a line opens its detail, with « Validate » and « Return » (reason required). Tick several lines, even of different modes or projects, then « Validate selection »: a single combined invoice is created. If the projects have different clients, you pick the invoice’s client. After approval, the draft invoice opens to be completed.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.CREDIT_TEXT: Credit notes created from an invoice file arrive here. « Validate » approves and issues it (number AV-…), « Return » sends it back to its author. A click opens its invoice file.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.HISTORY_TEXT: The latest 200 decisions: date, user, action (approval, return, cancelled approval), item and comment, with search and filters.
APPROVAL_QUEUE.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

APPROVAL_DETAIL.INTRO_TEXT: A billing line or a deliverable batch awaiting approval: what you need to decide. This guide opens the tabs by itself and gives yours back at the end.
APPROVAL_DETAIL.HEADER_TEXT: The billed period as title, the status and mode as badges; the breadcrumb leads back to the approval queue.
APPROVAL_DETAIL.IDENTITY_TEXT: Project, client, period, billing date, mode, project status, budget and manager. If the request was returned, the « Return reason » shows.
APPROVAL_DETAIL.ACTIONS_TEXT: While the request is pending: « Validate » creates the draft invoice and opens it to be completed; « Return » sends it back with a required reason, for correction. « View project » opens its file.
APPROVAL_DETAIL.KPIS_TEXT: For a line: amount excl. tax (with VAT), incl. tax, WIP amount and project total as % of budget. For a batch: amount excl. tax and number of entries, confirmed amount and carry-over from the previous period.
APPROVAL_DETAIL.TABS_TEXT: « Project history » (or « Entries » for a batch) and « Activity log ». The open tab is kept in the address (?tab=…).
APPROVAL_DETAIL.ITEMS_TEXT: For a line: every billing line of the project, the current request marked « Current ». For a batch: each document, its previous rate, its new rate and the amount.
APPROVAL_DETAIL.AUDIT_TEXT: Every action on the request: date, action, status before → after, author’s role and comment.
APPROVAL_DETAIL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

SUBCONTRACTING.INTRO_TEXT: Three levels: the subcontractor directory, the subcontracting orders (ST orders) placed on a project, and a project’s margin analysis. The guide opens each tab and gives yours back at the end.
SUBCONTRACTING.TABS_TEXT: Subcontractors, ST Orders and Cost analysis. A sentence under the tabs recalls what each holds. The open tab is kept in the address (?tab=…).
SUBCONTRACTING.ST_TEXT: The entity’s directory of external providers: indicators, search (name, e-mail, phone, tax ID), filters and grid or list view. « New subcontractor » (name required, unique in the entity), « Edit », « Deactivate ». A subcontractor must exist here before receiving an order.
SUBCONTRACTING.ENTITY_TEXT: This selector picks the entity whose directory is shown. It only applies to the Subcontractors tab; the other two follow the chosen project.
SUBCONTRACTING.ORDERS_TEXT: Search for then pick a project: its orders show with budget, spent, % consumed and status. « New ST order »: subcontractor, scope, budget, currency and alert threshold (10 % by default). The project must be In progress. « Status »: In progress, Suspended or Closed (final). CSV export.
SUBCONTRACTING.COSTS_TEXT: « Costs » opens an order’s cost panel: « Add a cost » (amount, date — not in the future —, description), only on an In progress order. Beyond budget + threshold, the order is flagged as over budget.
SUBCONTRACTING.ANALYSIS_TEXT: Pick a project: collected revenue (payments received), subcontracting costs, gross margin and margin rate, with the breakdown. Internal costs are not computed yet (always 0).
SUBCONTRACTING.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

COSTS.INTRO_TEXT: Your entity’s cost invoices: supplier invoices or expenses with no supplier, each with one or more lines. They go through an approval circuit, then get paid.
COSTS.KPIS_TEXT: Drafts, Pending (submitted) and Approved (including those already paid), counted on the page shown.
COSTS.NEW_TEXT: Opens a cost invoice form: supplier, lines, taxes, attachments.
COSTS.TOOLBAR_TEXT: The search covers the reference, the supplier and the invoice number. « Filters »: status, category, period and amount incl. tax (on the page shown). Three views: grid, list (sort by header) and suppliers, which groups the invoices by supplier.
COSTS.LIST_TEXT: Each invoice: reference (EXP-year-no.), supplier, supplier invoice number, categories, date, amounts excl. and incl. tax (and in EUR), status and approval level. A click opens its file; in the suppliers view, the supplier’s page.
COSTS.ACTIONS_TEXT: « Edit » and « Submit » on a draft; « Create a payment » on an approved invoice not yet paid; « View details » everywhere.
COSTS.LIFECYCLE_TEXT: Draft → « Submit »: the approval level is computed on the amount incl. tax in euros. Level L1: approved at once. L2 to L4: Submitted, waiting in the approval queue (L4: two approvers). Approved → payment recorded → Posted (paid). A request for more information or a refusal sends it back to Draft.
COSTS.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

COST_NEW.INTRO_TEXT: A supplier invoice, or an expense with no supplier, in one or more lines. It is saved as a draft or sent straight into the approval circuit.
COST_NEW.INVOICE_TEXT: Entity, supplier (optional), supplier invoice number — required with a supplier, only once per supplier —, invoice date, due date and currency.
COST_NEW.LINES_TEXT: Each line has its cost category (and sub-category), description, optional project (same entity) and amount excl. tax. With a supplier: FODEC and VAT per line; without: VAT as an amount. A part outside the VAT scope can be isolated (a travel agency’s plane ticket…).
COST_NEW.TAXES_TEXT: Stamp duty (once per invoice, with a supplier), withholding tax if ticked — deducted from the net payable —, and free other taxes added to the total. Totals excl. tax, VAT, incl. tax and net payable update as you type.
COST_NEW.ATTACH_TEXT: PDF, JPEG or PNG, 10 MB max per file. They are uploaded when the invoice is saved; they can no longer be added from the file.
COST_NEW.CIRCUIT_TEXT: The expected level based on the total converted to euros: automatic approval (L1), single approval or dual validation (L4), with the expected approvers.
COST_NEW.ACTIONS_TEXT: « Save draft » keeps the invoice without sending it; « Submit for approval » saves it and starts the circuit. The message in the middle says what is missing. « Cancel » leaves without saving.
COST_NEW.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

COST_EDIT.INTRO_TEXT: The same form, prefilled. A draft is freely editable (the entity can no longer change). An approved or paid invoice can only be edited with the CFO right, with a justification.
COST_EDIT.ACTIONS_TEXT: Draft: « Save draft » or « Submit for approval ». Validated invoice: « Save the change », after a justification of at least 5 characters; status and payment are kept, every change is logged.

COST_DETAIL.INTRO_TEXT: Everything about a cost invoice: its identity and actions on the left, its amounts and tabs on the right. The guide opens each tab and gives yours back at the end.
COST_DETAIL.HEADER_TEXT: The invoice reference, with its status and approval level; the breadcrumb leads back to the cost list.
COST_DETAIL.IDENTITY_TEXT: Supplier, invoice number, dates, currency, categories… Actions: « Edit » and « Submit for approval » on a draft, « New payment » on an approved invoice, « Edit (CFO) » on a validated invoice for those with the right.
COST_DETAIL.KPIS_TEXT: Excl. tax, VAT, incl. tax, their EUR equivalents and, with withholding tax, the net payable to the supplier.
COST_DETAIL.TABS_TEXT: Lines and totals, Approvals, Attachments, Change history, Reminders and Payment. The open tab is kept in the address (?tab=…).
COST_DETAIL.INFO_TEXT: Each line (category, project, description, excl. tax, taxes) then the invoice totals.
COST_DETAIL.APPROVALS_TEXT: Each decision of the circuit: level, author, date, decision (approved, more information, refused, auto-approved) and comment.
COST_DETAIL.ATTACHMENTS_TEXT: The invoice’s files, to download. They can only be deleted on a draft; they are added from the form.
COST_DETAIL.CHANGES_TEXT: Changes made after validation: author, date, justification and changed fields (before / after).
COST_DETAIL.REMINDERS_TEXT: Internal reminders before the due date of an approved, unpaid invoice, e-mailed every morning. They can be suspended (with a reason) and resumed.
COST_DETAIL.LEDGER_TEXT: The invoice’s payment and the supplier statement: amount paid against net payable, debit (overpaid), credit (still owed) and balance. A payment is edited or deleted here; Excel export.
COST_DETAIL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

COST_SUPPLIER.INTRO_TEXT: All of a supplier’s cost invoices and its payment statement. The guide opens the tabs and gives yours back at the end.
COST_SUPPLIER.IDENTITY_TEXT: Code, type, tax ID, country and number of invoices. « New invoice » opens the form with this supplier; « New payment » pays one of its approved invoices.
COST_SUPPLIER.KPIS_TEXT: The supplier and the totals of its cost invoices, all statuses.
COST_SUPPLIER.INVOICES_TEXT: The supplier’s cost invoices, all statuses; a click opens the file.
COST_SUPPLIER.LEDGER_TEXT: One row per paid invoice, by payment date: amount paid against net payable, debit (overpaid), credit (still owed) and running debit or credit balance. Approved unpaid invoices are not listed. Excel export.

COST_UNASSIGNED.INTRO_TEXT: Expenses entered with no supplier (no FODEC, stamp duty or withholding tax). There is no payment statement for them.

COST_APPROVAL.INTRO_TEXT: Three queues in one: submitted cost invoices, hiring requests costed by HR and salary advances validated by HR. Everyone only sees what their rights let them decide.
COST_APPROVAL.KPIS_TEXT: Pending: the total of the three queues. Urgent: invoices of level L3 or L4.
COST_APPROVAL.TOOLBAR_TEXT: Free search, and « Filters »: request type, priority, level, category, date, currency and amount. Grid or list view.
COST_APPROVAL.LIST_TEXT: Each request shows its type, subject, amount and level. « View details » opens the file (cost invoice or candidate).
COST_APPROVAL.COSTS_TEXT: Submitted invoices, highest first. Decisions: « Approve » (optional comment), « More information » (sent back to draft to be completed) or « Refuse » (comment required, sent back to draft). At level L4, two different approvers are needed.
COST_APPROVAL.HIRING_TEXT: The salary cost of a hire costed by HR (monthly loaded cost × 12). Approve, or refuse with an optional counter-offer salary.
COST_APPROVAL.ADVANCES_TEXT: Advances validated by HR, awaiting the finance decision. Approve (payroll then pays it out) or refuse with a reason. You cannot decide your own advance.
COST_APPROVAL.NEW_TEXT: Opens the form of a new cost invoice.
COST_APPROVAL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

COST_MISSIONS.INTRO_TEXT: The final decision on mission costs: created by a manager, costed and validated by HR, they arrive here awaiting the finance decision.
COST_MISSIONS.KPIS_TEXT: Awaiting decision, Imminent departures (within 3 days, or already started) and International missions.
COST_MISSIONS.TOOLBAR_TEXT: Free search and filters; grid or list view.
COST_MISSIONS.LIST_TEXT: Each mission: employee, destination, dates, urgency and estimated cost (allowances, lodging, ticket, visa, insurance, other fees; the cash advance is not counted).
COST_MISSIONS.DECIDE_TEXT: Open a mission: mission and expense details, HR notes. « Approve the cost » or « Refuse » (reason required).
COST_MISSIONS.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

RATES.INTRO_TEXT: Scales compute, for each employee, an intercompany rate and a time & materials selling rate. The latest validated scale applies.
RATES.PAYS_TEXT: Pick the entity whose scales you manage.
RATES.FORMULA_TEXT: Interco rate = cost × (1 + % HQ); selling rate = cost × (1 + % HQ + % margin), recalled above the table.
RATES.TABLE_TEXT: Each scale: period (month, quarter or year), type, % HQ, % margin, interco and external margins, currency, status and validation date. Expand one to see its lines per employee.
RATES.NEW_TEXT: « + New scale »: pick the period and percentages. The scale starts as Draft.
RATES.LIFECYCLE_TEXT: « Auto-fill from formula » creates one line per active employee from the period’s paid costs. « Compute » moves the scale to Computed (daily, hourly, monthly, interco and external rates). « Validate » locks it.
RATES.ALLOCATION_TEXT: This button opens the cost category allocation: per headcount (total ÷ number of employees), fixed amount, or direct (costs tied to the employee). It drives auto-fill.
RATES.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

EMPLOYEE_COSTS.INTRO_TEXT: Each employee’s cost over a period: base cost to the company, internal selling cost and external selling cost. They feed time & materials and rate scales.
EMPLOYEE_COSTS.KPIS_TEXT: Tracked employees (active / expired share), average selling costs (internal, interco, external) and average margins.
EMPLOYEE_COSTS.TOOLBAR_TEXT: Search by employee, Active / Expired filter and other criteria; grid or list view.
EMPLOYEE_COSTS.LIST_TEXT: One row per employee and period: base, internal and external costs, currency, dates and status. Only an employee’s latest period is « Active »; the others are « Expired ».
EMPLOYEE_COSTS.ACTIONS_TEXT: « Edit », « Delete » (permanent) and « History », which opens this cost’s log.
EMPLOYEE_COSTS.ADD_TEXT: « Add »: employee, period and one of the three amounts — the others are computed (internal = base × 1.1; external = base × 1.2). Two periods of the same employee cannot overlap.
EMPLOYEE_COSTS.EXPORT_TEXT: « Export Excel » downloads the filtered list.
EMPLOYEE_COSTS.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

EMPLOYEE_COST_HISTORY.INTRO_TEXT: Everything that happened to an employee’s cost: creations, changes, deletions and status changes. The breadcrumb leads back to the list.
EMPLOYEE_COST_HISTORY.TOOLBAR_TEXT: Search and filters (action, period…); two layouts: timeline or table.
EMPLOYEE_COST_HISTORY.LIST_TEXT: Each event: date, action, author and changed fields with their before and after values.
EMPLOYEE_COST_HISTORY.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

SUPPLIERS.INTRO_TEXT: Your entity's suppliers, to which cost invoices are attached. Each record holds the supplier's identity, tax details and IBAN.
SUPPLIERS.NEW_TEXT: Opens the three-step creation wizard: identification, tax details, bank details.
SUPPLIERS.KPIS_TEXT: Number of active suppliers, those with an IBAN (needed for a transfer), those with a VAT number, and the countries covered. They describe the entity's whole active register, not the page shown nor the search.
SUPPLIERS.TOOLBAR_TEXT: « Filters »: supplier type, presence of an IBAN or a VAT number. The search covers name and code. The toggle switches between cards and a table you can sort by header.
SUPPLIERS.STATUS_TEXT: Only active suppliers are listed by default. The « Status » filter (Deactivated or All) brings deactivated suppliers back; a banner says so.
SUPPLIERS.LIST_TEXT: Each supplier: name, country, type, VAT number, IBAN and status. A click opens its record.
SUPPLIERS.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

SUPPLIER_NEW.INTRO_TEXT: Three steps; only the first is mandatory. The guide previews each step without saving anything.
SUPPLIER_NEW.HEADER_TEXT: The title, the breadcrumb and, as chips, a summary of what you've entered so far.
SUPPLIER_NEW.RAIL_TEXT: The wizard's three steps. You can click a step you've already passed to go back, not jump ahead.
SUPPLIER_NEW.S1_TEXT: Company name, country and supplier type, all mandatory. The country sets the prefix of the supplier's code, assigned automatically on creation.
SUPPLIER_NEW.S2_TEXT: VAT number — unique: a number already used, in any country, makes the save fail —, tax ID, and calculation profile: Standard (net + rate) or Travel agency, which changes how its cost invoices are entered.
SUPPLIER_NEW.S3_TEXT: The IBAN, used for bank-transfer payments. Optional, but a supplier without an IBAN cannot be paid by transfer.
SUPPLIER_NEW.NEXT_TEXT: « Next » moves to the next step (step 1 must be complete); on the last step, « Create supplier » saves it and opens its record.
SUPPLIER_NEW.BACK_TEXT: « Back » returns to the previous step without losing anything; « Cancel », on the first step, leaves without saving.
SUPPLIER_NEW.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

SUPPLIER_EDIT.INTRO_TEXT: The same wizard, prefilled with the supplier's record. Nothing is saved before the last step.
SUPPLIER_EDIT.S1_TEXT: Company name and type can change. The country stays visible but locked: the supplier's code depends on it.
SUPPLIER_EDIT.NEXT_TEXT: « Next » moves to the next step; on the last one, « Save » applies the changes and returns to the record.
SUPPLIER_EDIT.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

SUPPLIER_DETAIL.INTRO_TEXT: Its identity and actions on the left, its figures and tabs on the right. The guide opens each tab and gives you yours back at the end.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.HEADER_TEXT: The supplier's name, code and country, and its status (active or deactivated); the breadcrumb leads back to the list.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.IDENTITY_TEXT: Identification (code, country, type, creation date), tax details (VAT number, tax ID) and bank details (IBAN). Missing data is flagged.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.ACTIONS_TEXT: « New supplier invoice » opens a cost invoice already linked to this supplier; « Edit » reopens the wizard; « View costs » opens the supplier view of the Costs module. Creating and editing require the right to manage costs.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.DEACTIVATE_TEXT: Removes the supplier from the list and the search; its invoices and history are kept. Note: there is no reactivation.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.KPIS_TEXT: Number of invoices and their gross total in euros (all statuses), then the number of statement entries and the balance due — or the overpayment — from the last statement entry.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.TABS_TEXT: « Invoices » lists its cost invoices, « Payment » its account statement. The open tab is kept in the page's address.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.COSTS_TEXT: The supplier's cost invoices, read-only: search, filters and export. A click opens the invoice's record, where submission, approval and payment happen.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.LEDGER_TEXT: The account statement: each paid invoice as debit and credit, with the running balance. Only paid invoices appear.
SUPPLIER_DETAIL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

REPORTING.INTRO_TEXT: Each country's monthly income statement: one period per month, closed to freeze its figures, then a report that goes Submitted → Endorsed (CD) → Accepted (Group).
REPORTING.ACTIONS_TEXT: The country selector (if you follow several) and the « Actions » menu: New period (with the right to manage costs), Submission calendar and Reference budget.
REPORTING.KPIS_TEXT: The year's net revenue, EBITDA and EBITDA margin, summed over closed periods only — an open month is not counted. « Reports to process »: those to endorse, to accept or sent back for amendment.
REPORTING.TOOLBAR_TEXT: Search on the period label; filters by year, period status and report status. Cards or table.
REPORTING.LIST_TEXT: Each month: its progress, net revenue, EBITDA and % (red when negative), and the state of its report. A click opens the report.
REPORTING.LIFECYCLE_TEXT: New period (one per country and month) → « Close »: the month's figures are frozen, with manual inputs (intercompany, intersede, WIP, recharges) → « Generate report » → approval circuit from the report's page.
REPORTING.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

PL_BUDGET.INTRO_TEXT: A country's annual budget, month by month and line by line of the group catalogue. It is the basis of the budget variances in P&L reports.
PL_BUDGET.FILTERS_TEXT: Choose the country (if you follow several) and the budget year to show.
PL_BUDGET.CREATE_TEXT: If there is no budget yet for this country and year, « Create the budget » opens one (right to manage the P&L).
PL_BUDGET.GRID_TEXT: One row per catalogue line, one column per month. An empty cell counts as zero. Without the right to manage, the grid is read-only.
PL_BUDGET.SAVE_TEXT: Saves the whole grid. A P&L report takes the budget as it stands when the report is generated.
PL_BUDGET.APPROVALS_TEXT: Two approvals: Country Director then Group, reserved to P&L administrators. Each shows its date and author once given.
PL_BUDGET.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

PL_CALENDAR.INTRO_TEXT: The P&L report submission deadlines, one per month.
PL_CALENDAR.YEAR_TEXT: Choose the year whose deadlines you want to see.
PL_CALENDAR.TABLE_TEXT: For each month: the deadline, who set it and when.
PL_CALENDAR.EDIT_TEXT: With the right to administer the P&L: pick the date then « Save » on the row. The deadline is indicative: it does not block submission and sends no reminder.
PL_CALENDAR.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

REPORT_DETAIL.INTRO_TEXT: A country's report for one month: its details and actions on the left, its figures and tabs on the right. The guide opens each tab and gives you yours back at the end.
REPORT_DETAIL.HEADER_TEXT: The report's country and month, its version and status; the breadcrumb leads back to the P&L dashboard.
REPORT_DETAIL.IDENTITY_TEXT: Country, period, period status, version and creation date; then the submission, endorsement (CD) and acceptance (Group) dates.
REPORT_DETAIL.ACTIONS_TEXT: The main button depends on the status and your rights: « Submit » (draft or amendment requested), « Endorse » (submitted, Country Director), « Accept » (endorsed, Group). If nothing is yours to do, the card says so.
REPORT_DETAIL.AMEND_TEXT: « Amendment » sends a submitted or endorsed report back to preparation, with a reason. « Reopen » an accepted report: new version (the current one is archived) or correction absorbed by the next month, with a justification.
REPORT_DETAIL.EXPORTS_TEXT: The report as Excel or PDF, or the full 7-sheet workbook.
REPORT_DETAIL.KPIS_TEXT: The month's gross revenue 2, net revenue, EBITDA and EBITDA %, as frozen when the period was closed.
REPORT_DETAIL.TABS_TEXT: Overview, P&L recap, Commentaries and Treasury. The open tab is kept in the page's address.
REPORT_DETAIL.OVERVIEW_TEXT: The waterfall from revenue to EBITDA, the workflow's progress, the number of commentaries written and the month's cost breakdown.
REPORT_DETAIL.RECAP_TEXT: Each catalogue line: actual, budget and variance. Search and filters (positive, negative variance, no budget, amount).
REPORT_DETAIL.COMMENTS_TEXT: Variance commentaries, line by line, then the cross-cutting summary (revenue, costs, EBITDA, other points). A text is proposed; with the right to manage the P&L, you correct it then save it.
REPORT_DETAIL.TREASURY_TEXT: The country's open customer receivables by age, and missing cash per project (receivables plus unbilled WIP).
REPORT_DETAIL.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

TREASURY.INTRO_TEXT: What should come in (unpaid customer invoices) and go out (committed cost invoices), month by month, for your entity. It is a flow projection, not a bank balance.
TREASURY.HORIZON_TEXT: Projection over 3, 6 or 12 months from the current month.
TREASURY.KPIS_TEXT: Overdue receivables (unpaid at due date, over the last 90 days), expected receipts up to the end of the horizon, committed payments (submitted or approved cost invoices, less recorded payments). Hover a tile for details.
TREASURY.LOW_POINT_TEXT: The tightest moment: where cumulative inflows minus outflows are lowest. It is the main question this page answers.
TREASURY.CHARTS_TEXT: Two charts on the same scale, so heights compare at a glance. They show upcoming months, without what is already overdue.
TREASURY.TABLE_TEXT: An « Already overdue » row then one per month: receipts, payments, net and cumulative. The low-point month is flagged. The cumulative starts at zero: it is a change from today.
TREASURY.FLOWS_TEXT: Expected receipts on the left, committed payments on the right: counterparty, due date (and delay), converted amount with the original amount below. A click on a receipt opens its collection file.
TREASURY.LIMITS_TEXT: No opening balance, no salaries or taxes, past due dates kept for 90 days only, conversion at the current rate. The « collected over 30 days » marker gives an actual order of magnitude.
TREASURY.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

ADMIN.INTRO_TEXT: The Finance module settings, in tabs. The guide only opens the tabs your rights show, and gives you yours back at the end.
ADMIN.PAYS_TEXT: If you manage several countries, choose here the entity whose settings you change (lists, currencies, cost configuration).
ADMIN.TABS_TEXT: Each tab groups one kind of setting. Which ones you see depends on your rights.
ADMIN.LISTS_TEXT: The values offered in the screens (cost categories, supplier types…), by family. A « Global » value applies to all entities; adding, editing or deactivating here only affects the chosen entity.
ADMIN.FOREX_TEXT: The rates to the euro (and Swiss franc) used to convert amounts: approval circuits, P&L, treasury. Without a CHF rate, it is EUR × 0.965. A currency without a rate is left out of totals.
ADMIN.FOREX_API_TEXT: The provider that can refresh rates automatically (working days at 8 am, if auto-refresh is on), and a button to refresh them now.
ADMIN.ENTITY_CURRENCY_TEXT: The default currency of each ARX entity, chosen among the active currencies of the « Currency » list.
ADMIN.COST_CONFIG_TEXT: Cost invoice approval thresholds (levels L1 to L4) and the Costs module's list values, for the chosen entity.
ADMIN.REMINDERS_TEXT: Customer invoice reminder steps: X days before or after the due date, recipients (roles, customer) and message. A run goes out daily at 8 am. « Trigger now » sends the due reminders right away, with real e-mails.
ADMIN.COST_REMINDERS_TEXT: Internal reminders to pay suppliers on time, based on each cost invoice's due date, sent to the given roles.
ADMIN.PERMISSIONS_TEXT: Each role's Finance rights. A change takes effect at the user's next sign-in.
ADMIN.DOC_TEMPLATES_TEXT: The HTML layout of PDF documents. Today only the « Invoice — AV mode (fixed price) » template is used, for the draft preview.
ADMIN.WIP_EMAILS_TEXT: Subject and body of the e-mail sent to the customer when a progress, timesheet or deliverable is validated. A country template takes precedence over the global one.
ADMIN.AUDIT_TEXT: The history of changes to Finance data: who, when, what, with before / after details.
ADMIN.HELP_FAQ_TEXT: Your own questions / answers, page by page, on top of the shipped FAQ. Once published, they show at the top of the chosen page's FAQ, in « Help & guides » as in the help assistant. French is required, English optional.
ADMIN.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

ADMIN_ROLES.INTRO_TEXT: The Finance rights granted to each role. Roles themselves and their assignment to users are managed in the HR module.
ADMIN_ROLES.LIST_TEXT: Each role with its number of permissions. The search filters the list.
ADMIN_ROLES.OPEN_TEXT: A click on a role opens its permissions; the breadcrumb leads back to the list.
ADMIN_ROLES.GROUPS_TEXT: Permissions sorted by group, with the count of checked ones. Check or uncheck each right; Finance rights (FACT_…) are tinted.
ADMIN_ROLES.BULK_TEXT: Shortcuts over the whole catalogue. Careful: unchecking all then saving removes every right of the role, administration included.
ADMIN_ROLES.SAVE_TEXT: Applies the changes. They take effect at the role's users' next sign-in.
ADMIN_ROLES.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

ADMIN_DOC_TEMPLATES.INTRO_TEXT: The HTML layout of PDFs generated by invoicing, per document type. Today only the « Invoice — AV mode (fixed price) » template is used, for the draft preview.
ADMIN_DOC_TEMPLATES.ACTIONS_TEXT: Also show inactive templates, filter by document type, and « New template ».
ADMIN_DOC_TEMPLATES.TABLE_TEXT: Each template: name, description, type, state. Actions: edit, activate or deactivate.
ADMIN_DOC_TEMPLATES.EDITOR_TEXT: Type, name, description and HTML code of the template. « Insert default template » starts from a complete layout.
ADMIN_DOC_TEMPLATES.VARIABLES_TEXT: Click a variable to insert it at the cursor: it will be replaced by the invoice's data (customer, amounts, lines…).
ADMIN_DOC_TEMPLATES.PREVIEW_TEXT: Enter an invoice's id to see the PDF with its data, or leave it empty for mock data.
ADMIN_DOC_TEMPLATES.ACTIVE_TEXT: There should be one active template per type: activating one deactivates the others. A newly created template is active straight away.
ADMIN_DOC_TEMPLATES.END_TEXT: Restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu, or ask the assistant.

LIST.SUBTITLE: Manage your customer invoice issuance and tracking.

ERROR.MARK_SENT: Could not mark the invoice as sent.
ERROR.APPROVE: Could not submit the approval decision.

AUDIT.NO_FIELD_CHANGES: No field changes were recorded for this entry.

NEW.SUBTITLE: Build the invoice, step by step.
NEW.LEAVE_BODY: The invoice has not been saved. Leaving cancels the approval: the draft invoice is deleted and the request goes back to the approval queue.

AFFAIRE.TITLE: Invoice initialization
AFFAIRE.SUB: Select the relevant project and the type of document to generate.

LINES.TITLE: Billing lines
LINES.SUB: Add services, quantities and amounts to invoice.

CONDITIONS.TITLE: Payment conditions
CONDITIONS.SUB: Set the payment terms and due date.

RECAP.TITLE: Summary & Validation
RECAP.SUB: Review information before creating the invoice.

HELP.TITLE: Need help?
HELP.TEXT: The project is the single entry point for your invoicing. If you can't find your project, make sure it is activated in the Projects module.

TIPS.AFFAIRE: Select the relevant project. The available RAF is checked automatically to prevent over-billing.
TIPS.LINES: Add each service with its quantity, unit price ex. tax and applicable VAT rate.
TIPS.CONDITIONS: Set the due date, payment terms and purchase order if required for this billing type.
TIPS.RECAP: Review all information before submitting or saving as a draft to come back later.

LIFECYCLE.EMIT_DATE_HINT: Date printed on the invoice — today by default.

STEP_AFFAIRE.SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER: Search by name or project number…
STEP_AFFAIRE.NO_INVOICE_TYPE: No active invoice type for this affaire's country. Add some under Administration › Invoice types.
STEP_AFFAIRE.COMBINED_HINT: This invoice groups lines from several affaires, validated together from the approval queue. The lines are shown in the next step.
STEP_AFFAIRE.COMBINED_SAME_AFFAIRE_HINT: This invoice groups several billing-mode lines for the same affaire, validated together from the approval queue. The lines are shown in the next step.

STEP_LINES.TITLE: Billing lines
STEP_LINES.ERROR: All lines must be filled in correctly.
STEP_LINES.REMBOURSABLE_EMPTY: No reimbursable expense available for this currency.
STEP_LINES.REMBOURSABLE_LINES_TITLE: Reimbursable expenses added to this invoice
STEP_LINES.CARRY_FORWARD_EMPTY: No uninvoiced WIP balance available for this affaire.
STEP_LINES.CARRY_FORWARD_REMOVE_SOURCE: Remove this balance from the line

STEP_CONDITIONS.DUE_DATE_AUTO_HINT: Calculated automatically from the payment conditions — editable.
STEP_CONDITIONS.BDC_REQUIRED_ERROR: PO required for this billing type.

CREDIT_NOTE_MODAL.TITLE: Issue a credit note
CREDIT_NOTE_MODAL.PARTIAL_NOT_SUPPORTED: Partial credit notes are not supported yet: leave this field empty, or enter the full invoice amount.
CREDIT_NOTE_MODAL.SAVE_ERROR: Error while issuing the credit note.
CREDIT_NOTE_MODAL.AMOUNT_HINT: If blank, the credit note equals the total invoice amount.

CONTACTS.TITLE: Contacts
CONTACTS.SUB: As many contacts as needed — finance, engineering, administration… These are the people linked to affaires and receiving the invoices.
CONTACTS.EMPTY: No contact recorded for this client.
CONTACTS.AT_LEAST_ONE: At least one contact is required.
CONTACTS.EMAIL_DUPLICATE: Two contacts of this client share the same address.
CONTACTS.PRIMARY_HINT: Main point of contact — only one per client.
CONTACTS.NO_EMAIL_WARNING: None of these contacts has an e-mail address: this client's invoices cannot be sent to anyone.
CONTACTS.NO_EMAIL: No e-mail address — will not receive invoices
CONTACTS.EMAIL_HINT: Without an address, this contact will not receive any invoice.
CONTACTS.CONFIRM_DEACTIVATE_BODY: The contact will no longer be offered when linking an affaire. It stays visible in the history of invoices already sent, and can be reactivated.

LIST.TITLE: Client Management
LIST.SUBTITLE: Client portfolio: revenue, KYC and projects in progress.
LIST.LOAD_ERROR: Could not load the clients. Check your connection.

EMPTY.TITLE: No clients found
EMPTY.DESC: Adjust your filters or add a new client.

KYC.PENDING_TEXT: This client has not yet been KYC validated. Without this validation, no invoice can be issued to them.
KYC.TITLE: KYC approval
KYC.PENDING_HINT: This client has not been KYC-approved yet. Approval is required before any invoice can be issued.

CONFIRM.REVOKE_KYC_BODY: Revoke this client’s KYC approval? No invoice can be issued until it is approved again.
CONFIRM.DEACTIVATE_BODY: Deactivate this client? This can be undone.

FORM.SERVER_ERROR: An error occurred. Please try again.

TIPS.0: Enter the official company name. A client code will be generated automatically if you leave this field empty.
TIPS.1: The company details, then its contacts. Those are the people linked to affaires and receiving the invoices — an e-mail address per contact is therefore essential.
TIPS.2: The payment term and currency will be applied by default to all this client's projects.

NEW.LOAD_ERROR: Could not load this client. Please try again.
NEW.TITLE: Create a new client
NEW.SUBTITLE: Fill in the client details, step by step.

LIST.TITLE: Projects
LIST.SUBTITLE: Portfolio tracking: budget, remaining and status of every project.
LIST.LOAD_ERROR: Could not load the projects. Check your connection.

DELETE.TITLE: Delete draft
DELETE.BODY: Draft {{reference}} — {{intitule}} will be removed from the project list. Its reference will not be reused.

TS.DELETE_HINT: The item is set to Cancelled: it stays visible with its history but no longer counts in the budget.
TS.DELETE_ERROR: Error while deleting the additional work.

OVERVIEW.NO_TS: No additional work recorded for this project.
OVERVIEW.HEALTH_HELP: Share of the forecast budget already COLLECTED: sum of payments received over the budget. The pill instead rates risk from the billing rate against the project's watch threshold — the two run in opposite directions, hence two colour scales.
OVERVIEW.TEAM_HELP: The project managers, one entry per person. The same person can hold several rows in the database (one per activity): the count shown is of distinct PEOPLE, not rows. Photos come from the HR module.

CHARTS.SLIDE_MULTI_HINT: Ctrl + click to show several charts together
CHARTS.HELP_INVOICED: Sum of the gross amounts (incl. tax) of issued invoices, on their issue date, whatever their status — the original invoicing chart. In per-period view, the dashed line is the forecast budget spread linearly over the project duration, per month, quarter or year: it is not an entered target. In cumulative view, it is the budget (plus integrated additional work when included).
CHARTS.HELP_WIP: The WIP declared in the WIP and Additional work WIP tabs, stacked by status: invoiced (approved by finance), pending (client or finance, including the client balance not yet carried over) and rejected / cancelled. A declaration counts in the month its period ends. Over the whole project, additional work included and every status ticked, the bars add up to the WIP tile. Billing modes other than Fixed price, Time & materials and Deliverables only declare additional work WIP.
CHARTS.HELP_PAYMENTS: Payments received on the project's invoices, on their payment date. Over the whole project, they add up to the collected amount of the « Project health » gauge. In cumulative view, the dashed line is the budget (plus integrated additional work when included).
CHARTS.HELP_COMPARE: The series picked with Ctrl + click, side by side per period, in the order money flows: declared WIP (net of tax, ticked statuses), invoiced (incl. tax, issued invoices on their issue date) and collected (incl. tax, payments on their payment date). Bars are grouped, not stacked: WIP is net of tax and the other two include tax, so they cannot be subtracted from one another. When invoiced and collected are shown together, the rate compares collected to invoiced, both incl. tax. In cumulative view, the dashed line is the budget (plus integrated additional work when included).
CHARTS.CMP_UNITS_NOTE: WIP net of tax; invoiced and collected incl. tax.
CHARTS.EMPTY_RANGE: No period of the project falls in this range.
CHARTS.WIP_TS_ONLY: This billing mode declares no WIP: only additional work WIP appears here.

KPI.CA_HELP: Sum of this project's invoices whose status is 'Collected'. The exact complement of 'Total invoiced': together they make up everything invoiced. A part-payment on an invoice that is still partly paid does not count here.
KPI.RAF_HELP: What is left to invoice: budget + integrated additional work − issued invoices. The percentage is the share still available. Negative = overrun.
KPI.WIP_HELP: Fixed-price: sum of the “Invoiced” column of the rate history (WIP tab), all rows included. T&M/Deliverable: sum of EVERY WIP entry in the WIP tab (whatever its status) − Total invoiced; negative = more was invoiced than the declared WIP. In all three cases, the sum of the “Invoiced” column of the TS WIP tab is added. 0 for other billing modes.
KPI.MARGIN_HELP: (Collected − subcontracting) / collected: a % of revenue, not of budget. Internal costs are 0 for lack of timesheets, so it is overstated.
KPI.BACKLOG_HELP: What is left of the contract to invoice: forecast budget − Total invoiced (the neighbouring tile). The pill is the share of the budget still in backlog. Negative = overrun.
KPI.INVOICED_HELP: Sum of this project's invoices whose status is not 'Collected' — the invoiced amount still owed. This is the reference 'invoiced' figure: Backlog and WIP are both computed from it.

HELP.OVERDUE_IN: Invoices past their payment date and not settled, over the last {{n}} days. Beyond that it is a collections matter, not a cash forecast.
HELP.EXPECTED_IN: What is left to collect before the end of the horizon, net of payments already received. Credit notes are not counted.
HELP.EXPECTED_OUT: Approved spend falling due, less supplier payments already recorded. Approved spend that nobody has marked as paid still counts as owed.
HELP.LOW_POINT: The tightest moment in the projection: where inflows minus outflows, accumulated, sit at their lowest. This is the question the page exists to answer.
HELP.CHART_IN: Expected inflows month by month. Same scale as the outflows chart, so the two heights can be compared by eye.
HELP.CHART_OUT: Committed outflows month by month. Same scale as the inflows chart.

TREASURY.WARN_NO_RATE: No exchange rate is configured for: {{devises}}. Flows in those currencies are excluded from every total on this page. Add the rate under Administration › Currencies to bring them back in.
TREASURY.DISCLAIMER: A flow projection, not a bank balance: the module holds no opening cash position, so the cumulative column reads as a variation starting today. Outflows are spend commitments — cost lines carry no settlement flag — and past due dates are only picked up over {{lookback}} days, for money in as well as money out. Amounts are converted to {{devise}} at the current rate. Actual benchmark: {{collected}} collected over the last 30 days.
